sections.h2: What the Eaton County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
Eaton County's register keeps the county's land title file: deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and any other paper that touches real estate between Charlotte, Grand Ledge, Eaton Rapids and the townships around them. Each filing is checked against Michigan's recording rules and then stored as a digital image.

Nobody at the counter will write a deed for you. Responsibility for wording and purpose rests with the person who prepared the paper, and legal questions go to an attorney. If a deed still has to be written, a title company or real estate lawyer can do it, and the signed original comes here afterward.

The counter opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, with the staff away from noon until 1:00. Courthouse holidays interrupt that schedule, so check the register's page before a holiday week. Anything sent by mail should include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, because the office requires one before it sends documents back.

A flat $30 covers each deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified real estate copy. The extras are itemized on the county's fees page.

Eaton County register charges
ServiceCharge
Filing one deed, mortgage or similar paper$30
Each further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges$3 each
Tax certificate, first 25 legal descriptions$5
Each description past that$0.20
Ordinary copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 a page
Certified copy of a recorded document$1 a page plus $5 for the seal

The website does not sell certified copies. Ask at the counter or write to the office.

sections.h2: When does a deed need the treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, a land contract or an assignment of one cannot go on the record until the county treasurer's office has certified the parcel. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate shows that nobody holds a tax lien or tax title on the land and that five years of taxes before the instrument date are settled.

The statute excuses quitclaim deeds and other conveyances without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds. The closer normally orders the certificate while escrow is open, so most sellers never request it directly.

A complete filing package has these pieces:

  • The treasurer's certificate stapled to a warranty deed or land contract.
  • The full price printed on the deed, or a value affidavit attached.
  • An addressed envelope with postage when the package travels by mail.
  • The $30 filing charge plus $5 for the certificate where one is required.

If you file by mail rather than through your closer, a simple order works well:

  1. Get the treasurer certificate first if the deed carries warranty language.
  2. Check that the price or value affidavit is on the deed.
  3. Add a check for the $30 charge, plus $5 for the certificate.
  4. Enclose a stamped envelope addressed to yourself.
  5. Send it to the register in Charlotte and watch for the recorded copy.

A package missing any piece comes back to the sender, and that can set a closing back by days. A parcel with unpaid taxes does not get a clean certificate until the balance is cleared.

A sale triggers two separate charges. The state charge is $3.75 per $500 of price (MCL 207.525). Eaton County adds 55 cents per $500, the rate set for counties under two million residents (MCL 207.504). Any leftover part of a $500 block is billed as a full block.

The law puts both on the grantor (MCL 207.502 and 207.523), and the state portion is due at the treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Your purchase contract may shift the cost to the buyer, but the statute still lists the seller as the one responsible.

Ask your closer to total both levies on the settlement statement before the closing date, so the figure is no surprise at the table.

Plenty of deeds owe no transfer tax, provided the document itself names the exemption it relies on. Counties follow MCL 207.505 and the state follows MCL 207.526, and the two lists agree except for the last family item below.

  • A price under $100.
  • Mortgages and other security papers, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Leases and leasehold transfers.
  • Court orders that move title without naming a price.
  • Quitclaim deeds fixing a flaw in title the grantee already holds.
  • Land contracts until legal title actually passes.
  • State tax only: a gift deed running from parent to child or stepchild, or grandparent to grandchild.

If tax was paid on a deal that qualified, MCL 207.523(4) lets the seller, or a buyer who paid in the seller's place, ask the state Department of Treasury for the money back.

sections.h2: Searching Eaton County land records online
sections.html:
The search link on the register's page reaches every record from 1836 up to the most recent proof date, so a whole chain of title can be traced from home. A link for electronic filing sits beside it.

Electronic filing lets a title company submit the signed deed the same day with no courier. Ask your closer whether the file goes in that way and when the recorded copy will reach you. Money owed on a parcel is a separate matter, and the county treasurer runs its own search for it.

sections.h2: Eaton County housing and where the courthouse is
sections.html: Eaton County has 109,581 residents as of July 2025 and 48,090 housing units. About three in four homes are lived in by their owners, 74.2% to be exact. Median owner-occupied value is $216,900, and half of renters pay at least $1,092 a month. Charlotte holds the courthouse, and the register's counter is there. Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet and Potterville are the other cities, and part of Lansing falls inside the county lines.

sections.h2: What happens when Eaton County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent bills are the county treasurer's job, and the same office is the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay behind. Its page says over 2,000 foreclosures have been prevented since 2016 and links a chart of Michigan's foreclosure deadlines.

Payment can be made online once the parcel number and amount are found in the county's tax search. A 2.49% fee applies to cards, and parcels inside Lansing use their own link. A county land bank deals with vacant and foreclosed property.

An owner in that spot can still sell. The payoff comes out of the sale money, and the treasurer's certificate tells the closer what must clear first. Call the treasurer for a payoff figure before you list, and ask your closer to confirm it again near the closing date. A cash sale skips a lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the certificate is still needed before a warranty deed can be recorded.

faqs.q: Where is a deed filed in Eaton County?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds in Charlotte, the county seat. The register's page on eatoncounty.org gives the counter location. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:30, except for the noon hour.

faqs.q: How much does Eaton County charge for a filing?
faqs.a: It is $30 for each document. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments adds $3 per extra instrument, and a tax certificate is $5 for 25 descriptions or fewer.

faqs.q: Can an Eaton County deed be filed online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the e-record link on the register's page. Paper filings by mail need a stamped envelope addressed back to the sender.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Eaton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, by statute. A purchase agreement can assign the cost to the buyer. The state share reaches the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: How old are the records online?
faqs.a: They start in 1836 and run to the latest proof date. Certified copies are not sold on the website, so contact the register's office for those.
